question: Should OpenClaw support sandboxed requesters spawning ACP sessions by running ACP inside a sandbox, by adding a host-side bridge/proxy, or by folding this into the broader execution-backend placement contract?
rationale: The next step defines a sandbox-to-host execution boundary plus public config and model-facing tool semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security design.

options.title: Design Sandbox-Aware ACP Boundary
options.body: Define a narrow bridge or placement contract for ACP spawn, steer, and cancel with explicit auth, audit, workspace, secret, rate-limit, and cleanup rules before implementation.

options.title: Require Harnesses Inside Sandbox
options.body: Keep the current host-side ACP block and document running Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or other harnesses inside the OpenClaw sandbox container as the supported workflow.

options.title: Defer To Execution Backends
options.body: Keep this issue open as an acceptance case while the broader backend/profile placement design settles remote-worker security and lifecycle semantics.

recommendation.title: Design Sandbox-Aware ACP Boundary
recommendation.body: Define a narrow bridge or placement contract for ACP spawn, steer, and cancel with explicit auth, audit, workspace, secret, rate-limit, and cleanup rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest direct history on sessions_spawn and the ACP sandbox limitation, including the commit that extended the block to slash-command spawns.
